openings.claim: Removable opposed lateral stops may register the hatch without reproducing the corner-lift effect of tighter retention. This is a geometry-dependent proposal, not a demonstrated joint.
openings.delta: Change the sideways-load carrier from seal friction to padded strip contacts. Explore two removable rim saddles made from the four strips, six bolts/nuts and four pads; tether removable parts with supplied cord. Nearest rival: stronger strap retention increases friction sufficiently without harmful corner lift.
openings.prediction: If lateral registration is the useful mechanism, the hatch remains within 1 mm during the 20 N pull without increased opposite-corner lift. The rival instead requires additional retention tension. A disturbed final closure tests whether the stops tolerate the right-contact offset; failure there defeats the proposed robustness.
openings.probe: First check whether actual rim geometry allows removable saddles and complete opening clearance using only supplied tools and materials. If feasible, fabricate within ninety minutes. One technician performs and records ten numbered opening/closure/pull cycles in twenty minutes, using the scale, ruler and stopwatch; put the supplied 1 mm card at the right contact on cycle ten. Record marked-position displacement under load, corner lift, reopening time, visible seal condition and any maintenance. Inspect pads, fasteners and tethers each cycle. Stop for damage, but retain completed measurements: a fabrication-only stop supplies no outcome evidence. No second configuration receives ten-cycle validation within twelve total trials.
assumptions: Rim profile, pad behavior, strip stiffness and recoverable external tether locations are unspecified; attachment feasibility cannot be presumed.
The same technician must fabricate, operate, time and observe; no additional observer or equipment is available.

Displacement above 1 mm, inability to withstand 20 N, reopening above thirty seconds, seal tears, permanent fixture deformation or obstructed access defeat fit. Repair or retightening must be reported as maintenance, not hidden repeatability.

assessment: A bounded probe is available only after the attachment-resource question resolves. Ten cycles can test one configuration and the required disturbance; twenty minutes is a capacity ceiling, not proof that one technician can capture all measurements. The probe does not establish a method winner.
